title: Quasi-finite images of closed nowhere dense subsets
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a quasi-finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [pqf-def-quasifinite]. If $T\subseteq |Y|$ is closed and nowhere dense, then $f(T)\subseteq |X|$ is nowhere dense. Here a subset is nowhere dense when the interior of its closure is empty; no closedness of $f(T)$ is asserted. Empty schemes and the empty subset are allowed.

proof.text: For every affine open $V\subseteq X$, finite type in [pqf-def-quasifinite] and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] gives a finite affine open covering $f^{-1}(V)=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}U_i$. Put $g_i=f|_{U_i}:U_i\to V$ and $T_i=T\cap U_i$. Each $T_i$ is closed in $U_i$ and has empty interior: an open subset of $U_i$ contained in $T_i$ is also open in $Y$ and contained in the closed nowhere dense $T$, hence empty. Thus $T_i$ is nowhere dense in $U_i$. We will prove that each $g_i(T_i)$ is nowhere dense in $V$.

Check the hypotheses for affine factorization. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], the finite-type map $f$ induces a finite-type ring map on every affine pair. Affine opens of $U_i$ and $V$ are affine opens of $Y$ and $X$, and their section rings and induced maps are unchanged by restriction. The reverse implication of that same criterion makes $g_i$ locally of finite type. As a map between affine schemes it is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), so it is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $v\in V$, its set-theoretic fibre is $U_i\cap f^{-1}(v)$ with the subspace topology. Each singleton is open there since it is open in the original fibre. The fibre homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre] identifies this with isolation in the scheme fibre. Consequently $g_i$ is quasi-finite in the exact sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite](3).

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-affine-open-in-finite] to $g_i$, whose source and target are affine by construction and which is quasi-finite by step 2. Obtain an affine scheme $Z_i$, an open immersion $j_i:U_i\to Z_i$ and a finite map $\pi_i:Z_i\to V$ with $g_i=\pi_i\circ j_i$.

Put $C_i=\overline{j_i(T_i)}$ in $Z_i$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $j_i$ identifies $U_i$ with an open subset $O_i$ of $Z_i$. Since $T_i$ is closed in $U_i$, $C_i\cap O_i=j_i(T_i)$. If $H\subseteq C_i$ is open in $Z_i$, then $H\cap O_i$ is open in $O_i$ and contained in its nowhere dense subset $j_i(T_i)$, so it is empty. Every point of $H$ would then have the neighbourhood $H$ disjoint from $j_i(T_i)$, contradicting membership in its closure. Thus $H=\varnothing$ and $C_i$ is closed and nowhere dense. This is the elementary argument of Topology Tag 03J0 (lemma-image-nowhere-dense-open), including invariance under the displayed homeomorphism.

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-image-nowhere-dense] to the finite morphism $\pi_i$ and the closed nowhere dense $C_i$. Its statement gives a closed nowhere dense $\pi_i(C_i)$ in $V$. The inclusion $g_i(T_i)\subseteq\pi_i(C_i)$ implies $\overline{g_i(T_i)}\subseteq\pi_i(C_i)$, so $g_i(T_i)$ is nowhere dense. Only this inclusion is used; $g_i(T_i)$ need not be closed.

Now $f(T)\cap V=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}g_i(T_i)$. A finite union of nowhere dense sets is nowhere dense: for two such sets $A,B$, any open $H\subseteq\overline A\cup\overline B$ has $H\setminus\overline A$ open and contained in $\overline B$, hence empty; then $H\subseteq\overline A$ gives $H=\varnothing$. Induct on $n$, starting with the empty union. This proves the assertion on every affine $V$ (Topology Tag 03HO). Finally, for an open $V$, closure satisfies $\overline{f(T)}\cap V=\overline{f(T)\cap V}^{\,V}$: neighbourhoods of a point in $V$ may be intersected with $V$. If an open $H$ of $X$ lies in $\overline{f(T)}$, its intersection with every member $V$ of the affine cover is empty by the local result. Thus $H=\varnothing$, as required (Topology Tag 03HP). Empty schemes, empty $T$, and empty finite covers are included.
